apy.heading: Anthropology (APY)
apy.version_note: Current public chapter captured on 2026-10-11; no chapter edition is inferred from download-navigation labels.

APY 101.name: Introduction to Anthropology
APY 101.description: Surveys archaeological, cultural, biological and linguistic approaches to humanity.

review.rationale: The breadth expressly spans cultural interpretation and biological domain study.

APY 105.name: HIV: Sex, Science, and Society
APY 105.description: Examines HIV/AIDS through scientific, social and policy perspectives.

review.rationale: Medical science and societal responses are both explicit.

APY 109.name: Anthropology of Religion
APY 109.description: Studies lived religion through anthropological field methods and diverse traditions.

review.rationale: Religious practice and its cultural interpretation organize the course.

APY 201.name: Principles of Archaeology
APY 201.description: Introduces archaeological history, methods and theory through the global prehistoric record.

review.rationale: Interpreting past human societies is the central content.

APY 202.name: Principles of Cultural Anthropology
APY 202.description: Examines cultural systems including economics, kinship, politics, health and religion.

review.rationale: Social and cultural organization define the subject.

APY 203.name: Principles of Physical Anthropology
APY 203.description: Studies human biological origins, evolution and adaptation through fossils and primate comparison.

review.rationale: The focus is biological domain knowledge rather than cultural interpretation or AI methods.

APY 204.name: Principles of Linguistic Anthropology
APY 204.description: Uses linguistic principles to study language within cultural, ideological and political life.

review.rationale: Language's cultural and social functions organize the course.

APY 205.name: Medicine and Health Care in Society
APY 205.description: Analyzes medicine, illness and healing in historical and cultural contexts.

review.rationale: Social interpretation of health practices and power is central.

APY 230.name: The Sounds of the World's Languages
APY 230.description: Introduces phonetics through the sounds of human languages and acoustic methods.

review.rationale: The specific content is acoustic and linguistic domain analysis, not language-model computation.

APY 301.name: World Prehistory: From Caves to Quinoa
APY 301.description: Examines global prehistory and the development of complex societies and states.

review.rationale: Historical human organization establishes human context.

APY 306.name: Human Evolution
APY 306.description: Uses vertebrate fossils to investigate human biological and behavioral evolution.

review.rationale: Human evolutionary biology is the substantive domain.

APY 307.name: Human Adaptation
APY 307.description: Studies human biological adaptation to environmental stresses and the limits of performance.
APY 307.prerequisites: Prerequisite: APY 201 and APY 202 and APY 203 and BIL 101 and BIL 109 .

review.rationale: Biological adaptation and physiology organize the described analysis.

APY 309.name: Evolution of Human Behavior
APY 309.description: Investigates human behavioral evolution using fossils, primates and cross-cultural comparison.

review.rationale: Biological evolution and cultural variation both contribute explicitly.

APY 310.name: Primate Behavior and Adaptation
APY 310.description: Studies primate anatomy, behavior, distribution and ecological adaptation through evolution.

review.rationale: Primate biology is the main domain, without an asserted AI application.

APY 311.name: Cuba Culture, History, and Society
APY 311.description: Examines Cuban cultures and communities through history, migration and regional comparison.

review.rationale: Cultural practices, historical relationships and diverse perspectives establish human context.

APY 312.name: Primate Cognition
APY 312.description: Examines nonhuman primate cognition and its implications for human cognitive evolution.
APY 312.prerequisites: Prerequisite: APY 203 or APY 310 Or PHI 246 Or PSY 250 .

review.rationale: Cognition is studied as biological domain knowledge, not artificial-intelligence model design.

APY 315.name: Folk and Alternative Medicine: Psychedelic Plants in Cultural Context
APY 315.description: Examines plant medicines through cultural practice, history, law and research ethics.

review.rationale: The described emphasis is cultural and ethical interpretation of medicine.

APY 320.name: The Evolution of Language
APY 320.description: Examines contemporary accounts of the origins and development of human language.

review.rationale: The source establishes language history and interpretation, not computational language processing.

APY 340.name: Marine Archaeology
APY 340.description: Locates, excavates and studies submerged archaeological sites.

review.rationale: Practical underwater archaeological methods define the described activity.

APY 345.name: Blood and Chocolate: Ancient Civilizations of Mesoamerica
APY 345.description: Uses archaeology to examine pre-Columbian Mesoamerican cultures, especially the Maya.

review.rationale: Historical cultural interpretation is central.

APY 356.name: Florida Archaeology
APY 356.description: Studies archaeological evidence of Florida cultures from early settlement to colonization.

review.rationale: Past human cultures are the explicit subject.

APY 359.name: The Archaeology of Plastics
APY 359.description: Examines plastics through artifact analysis, environmental impacts and social and political meanings.

review.rationale: Environmental domain analysis and cultural interpretation receive explicit attention.

APY 360.name: Anthropology of Food
APY 360.description: Studies human diet through nutrition, evolution, food customs and skeletal evidence.

review.rationale: The description combines biological nutrition with cultural food practices.

APY 361.name: Gender and Language
APY 361.description: Investigates how language constructs gender across cultures.

review.rationale: Social and cultural analysis of language and gender establishes human context.

APY 362.name: The Languages of the World
APY 362.description: Compares the structures of languages across regions and linguistic families.

review.rationale: Human language comparison is the described subject; no computational method is asserted.

APY 376.name: Economic Anthropology
APY 376.description: Examines small-scale and nonmarket economies within broader social organization.

review.rationale: Social and economic relationships define the course.

APY 384.name: Caribbean Archaeology
APY 384.description: Traces Caribbean lifeways from initial settlement through complex societies and later migration.

review.rationale: Historical human communities and political organization are central.

APY 385.name: Caribbean Cultures
APY 385.description: Examines Caribbean social diversity, exchange, households and beliefs.

review.rationale: Cultural and social organization establish the subject.

APY 390.name: Dead Bodies & Bioethics
APY 390.description: Analyzes ethical questions surrounding human remains, including consent, ownership and public display.

review.rationale: Ethics and the social treatment of bodies are the organizing content.

APY 391.name: Gender in Ancient Cultures
APY 391.description: Uses archaeology to examine gender roles in ancient complex societies.

review.rationale: Historical and cross-cultural gender interpretation is central.

APY 392.name: Sex and Culture
APY 392.description: Compares sexuality, gender roles, marriage, reproduction and political relationships across cultures.

review.rationale: Social institutions and identities define the subject.

APY 393.name: Drugs and Culture
APY 393.description: Compares drug use across cultural settings.

review.rationale: The explicit emphasis is cultural practice rather than pharmacological mechanism.

APY 394.name: Comparative Religion
APY 394.description: Investigates religious belief systems through cross-cultural perspectives.

review.rationale: Religious and cultural interpretation is central.

APY 395.name: Gender, Race, and Class
APY 395.description: Analyzes intersecting gender, race and class identities and the institutions shaping perceived differences.

review.rationale: Identity, social construction and power establish human context.

APY 396.name: Youth Culture, Identity, and Globalization
APY 396.description: Examines urban youth cultures, identity, marginalization and violence within globalization.

review.rationale: Social experience and cultural practice are the substantive content.

APY 397.name: Violence and Ritual
APY 397.description: Uses ethnographic perspectives to analyze ritual, violence, symbols and political power.

review.rationale: Cultural meaning and political relationships organize the course.

APY 398.name: Coastal Cultures
APY 398.description: Examines fishing communities, environmental relationships, technology and maritime beliefs.

review.rationale: Community decision-making and cultural relationships to the environment are central.

APY 399.name: The Anthropology of Kinship and Family in America
APY 399.description: Studies kinship, families and emerging networks through examples from the Americas and Caribbean.

review.rationale: Social organization and ethnographic interpretation establish human context.

APY 413.name: Medical Anthropology
APY 413.description: Studies health and disease through heredity, environment, culture and evolutionary adaptation.

review.rationale: Biological disease ecology and cultural perspectives are both explicit.

APY 414.name: Human Osteology
APY 414.description: Identifies and interprets human skeletal characteristics, pathology and trauma.

review.rationale: Anatomical and forensic domain methods establish the subject.

APY 415.name: Forensic Anthropology II: Fieldwork
APY 415.description: Investigates human remains from crime scenes and disasters, including analysis and legal context.

review.rationale: Applied forensic investigation is the central activity.

APY 416.name: Bioarchaeology-Peopling the past
APY 416.description: Studies bodies within their spatial, cultural and historical setting through bioarchaeology.

review.rationale: The description links biological remains with cultural and historical interpretation.

APY 418.name: Seminar in Anthropology
APY 418.description: Examines varying topics across anthropology's biological, linguistic, archaeological and cultural branches.

review.rationale: The particular subject is unspecified across multiple domains; a single taxonomy label is not justified.

APY 419.name: Politics of the Past
APY 419.description: Debates how archaeology, politics, capitalism and discrimination shape representations of the past.

review.rationale: Political and cultural interpretation of history is the explicit focus.

APY 420.name: Archaeology, Architecture, and the City
APY 420.description: Examines ancient architecture's role in changing social and political relationships.

review.rationale: Architecture is studied through its historical human context.

APY 421.name: Interpreting Bodies
APY 421.description: Analyzes how bodies are represented, gendered, regulated and used for social validation or coercion.

review.rationale: Cultural representation and social power establish the subject.

APY 423.name: Paleopathology: Health and disease in ancient peoples
APY 423.description: Studies disease in preserved human remains and its relationships to culture, economics and politics.
APY 423.prerequisites: Prerequisite: APY 414 and APY 416 Or Instructor Permission.

review.rationale: Pathology and social explanation are both explicit.

APY 435.name: Anthropology of Nature and Environment
APY 435.description: Examines how ideas and practices concerning nature and biology shape contemporary life.

review.rationale: Cultural anthropology and political ecology organize the inquiry.

APY 485.name: Archeological Theory and Technique
APY 485.description: Examines theoretical traditions informing archaeological research and interpretation.

review.rationale: Theory for interpreting human pasts is the central content.

APY 501.name: Methods of Anthropological Research
APY 501.description: Develops research methods across cultural, archaeological, linguistic and biological anthropology.

review.rationale: The stated methodological range spans cultural interpretation and biological domain work; specific emphasis can vary.

APY 505.name: Museum Internship
APY 505.description: Develops museum methods and research skills through on-site internship work.

review.rationale: The explicit content is applied professional museum practice.

APY 512.name: Advanced Medical Anthropology
APY 512.description: Applies medical-anthropology theories and methods to human health and disease problems.

review.rationale: Health-domain problems and anthropological explanation are combined.
